chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Hariz, from Zurara and Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

We said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'Is the turban part of the shroud for the deceased?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No. Rather, the obligatory shroud is three garments and a complete garment, not less than that, which covers his entire body. So whatever increases beyond that is Sunnah, up to reaching five garments. So whatever increases beyond that is an innovation (bid'ah). And the turban is Sunnah.'
And he (peace be upon him) said: 'The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) ordered with the turban, and the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) was turbaned.'

And the Sheikh, Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), sent to us a dinar when Abu 'Ubaydah al-Hazza' died, while we were in Medina, and ordered us to buy him embalming material (hanut) and a turban, so we did it.
ai.seo_question: What is the minimum number of garments required for a valid Islamic shroud, and is the turban obligatory?
ai.summary: This hadith delineates the fiqh of the kafan, establishing the obligatory minimum as three garments plus one complete covering, while categorizing the turban as a recommended Sunnah rather than a fard component. It highlights the continuity of this practice through the Prophet’s example and the specific instruction of Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to purchase a turban for Abu Ubaydah al-Haddad, illustrating the Imams' emphasis on dignified burial attire beyond the strict legal minimum.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin usman, from Hareyz, from Zurara and Muhammad Bin Muslim who both said,

‘We said to Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The turban of the deceased, is from the enshrouding’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No. But rather, the Obligatory shroud is of three clothes and a complete cloth, not being less than it to cover his body, all of it. So whatever increase, so it is a Sunnah, up it reaching five clothes. So whatever increase, it would be an innovation. And the turban is a Sunnah’.
And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The Prophet<sup>saww</sup> ordered with the turban, and the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> was turbaned’.

The Sheykh Al-Sadiq<sup>asws</sup> sent a Dinar to us, when Abu Ubeyday Al-Haza’a died, and we were in Al-Medina, and ordered us that we should buy embalming material (camphor etc.), and a turban. So we did it’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Uthaman from Hariz from Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim who have said the following:

“Once we asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, if turban is part of shroud for a deceased. He (the Imam) said, ‘No, it is not part of it. The obligatory shroud consist of three pieces of cloths, one over all; the minimum of which must be large enough to cover the whole body and any extra is of the Sunnah up to five pieces and more than this is contrived.’
He (the Imam) said, ‘The Holy prophet commanded to prepare turban and it was prepared for the Holy prophet.’

The truthful shaykh, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, sent for us one dinar, when we were in al-Madinah at the time of the death of abu ‘Ubaydah al-Hadhdha’. He (the Imam) commanded us to buy for him hunut and turban which we did.”’
